fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Where We Are Headed and What to Withdraw From", "body": "Amandha Vollmer opens by describing days spent writing, prepping an End of COVID summit, making soap for her store and homeschooling her eleven year old. Her larger focus is on tribes splitting off vibrationally, and on what support she can pull out of the old structure each week and redirect into local community. She refuses the fifteen minute city and says she will not accept CBDCs. Chance Garton connects this to the early 1960s series The Prisoner, which he says already contains fifteen minute cities and a globalist allegory whose monster enemy is a weather balloon."}, {"title": "Protection Is a Frequency, Not a Shield", "body": "Both hosts of the conversation land on the claim that real protection is vibrational rather than physical. Amandha calls the aura the shield against EMF, psychic vampires and everything else, and cites Power vs. Force for the measured gap between the frequency of fear and the frequency of love, arguing that people at different frequencies eventually cannot even relate to one another. Chance Garton describes a year of biofield tunings he taught himself from Eileen McCusick's books, and calls the aura an intelligent filter. Amandha adds forest bathing on her fifty three acres as her own reset."}, {"title": "Cities Drain the Battery, Presence Refills It", "body": "Chance Garton offers a theory that the city inverts its own name because constant filtering of dissonant sound and other people's vibes spends the same life force that awareness runs on. Everything compartmentalized out of focus is energy lost, while a forest reads as one harmonious whole that needs no filtering. Amandha Vollmer agrees, noting that pain and illness lower the same battery so coping shrinks. She invokes Thich Nhat Hanh, whom she studied while learning Buddhism, on being present at every step of washing a dish, and describes cleaning her house as tidying her own energy."}, {"title": "Why AI Will Never Carry the Divine Spark", "body": "The two turn skeptical about technocracy. Amandha Vollmer calls Elon Musk's Neuralink chip a fantasy given how much background radiation is already being pumped out, and warns that tools like ChatGPT outsource thinking exactly when people should be reclaiming it. Chance Garton, a former IT worker, argues that added complexity guarantees more breakage, and suspects space budgets exist partly to delete money from a fiat system. Amandha says an AI can never become emotionally sentient because it cannot pick up scent, body language or subtle nuance, and Chance answers that lines of code are not smelling."}, {"title": "Karma, Numerology, and Taking Health Into Your Own Hands", "body": "Amandha Vollmer maps a life as karmic contracts arriving around age twelve, then dharmic service work once they clear. She reads her own life path as a thirty four seven, patience and trust, and tracks personal year numbers. Chance Garton names the same pattern with his catchphrase that the obstacles are the course, and ties satisfaction to the sacral chakra and self worth. Amandha notes that sin originally means debt. The talk closes on practical remedies, including Green Immediate, the clove DMSO recipe from her book The Healing Power of DMSO, Facelift in a Jar, and her new site yummy.doctor."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The naturopathic healer and all around thought-leader for truth, health, and freedom, Amandha Vollmer, joins InnerVerse! As the founder of the Yum Naturals Emporium, Amandha and her team handcraft unique botanical blends of the utmost quality. In this flow-state chat, we get to know one another and enjoy an explorative conversation down many inspired avenues.
